deliverables: Ongoing Scalus maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor and cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Foundational runtime components including reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: 9-month continuation funding for Scalus maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, JVM/JS/TS interoperability, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal requests ₳2,464,844 for 9 months, equivalent to about $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate, with no contingency.
The proposal says the ask was reduced from a previous ₳8.5M 12-month proposal to ₳2.464844M over 9 months, with the L1 node and third-party dependency-heavy work removed from scope.
Scalus is claimed to be used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm systems.
Scalus components are claimed to be embedded in Cardano Client Lib, YaciDevKit, MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution.
The document states Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js has more than 20,000 monthly downloads.

The proposal claims Dijkstra will introduce Plutus V4 support, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts that affect smart contract development, evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and workflows.
Delivery is described as milestone-based, administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
The proposal excludes a standalone L1 node, full L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Lantr Engineering claims every prior milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.

summary: The document presents a reduced treasury ask for continued Scalus maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime, with several strong adoption and execution claims but much of the material evidence presented as proposer assertion rather than detailed verification in the anchor text.
